source.text: וּ/בְנֵ֥י יָוָ֖ן אֱלִישָׁ֣ה וְ/תַרְשִׁ֑ישָׁ/ה כִּתִּ֖ים וְ/רוֹדָנִֽים׃ס

translation.text: And the sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim[a].

footnotes.text: The Masoretic Genesis 10:4 name is “Dodanim,” while this Hebrew Chronicles text has “Rodanim.” Selected Greek has “Rhodians” in both passages; selected Latin has “Dodanim” in both. These parallel and versional differences do not establish which Genesis name is earlier.

lexical_decisions.rationale: בְּנֵי is the construct plural of 'sons of.' In genealogical contexts it can denote descendants more broadly, but here the immediate list of named peoples/places conventionally represented as offspring is well served by the formal 'sons of,' preserving the genealogy style of Chronicles.

This is a proper name and should be transliterated per project philosophy ('Translate titles; transliterate names'). Although the referent is associated with the Greek world/Ionia, the text presents it as a personal/genealogical name.
Proper name; the final he is part of the name form here, not something requiring a distinct English rendering. Standard English transliteration is 'Tarshish.'
Proper ethnonym/place-name; transliterated in a readable modern form. 'Chittim' reflects older English orthography, but 'Kittim' better matches the Hebrew consonant כ in contemporary transliteration.

The Masoretic Text in Chronicles reads רוֹדָנִים ('Rodanim'). Genesis 10:4 has 'Dodanim,' likely reflecting a textual variation between dalet and resh. Since the source text here is Chronicles, the main text follows MT 'Rodanim,' while preserving the alternative in a footnote as a worthwhile parallel/textual note.

value.text: And the sons of Javan: Elishah[a], Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.

footnotes.text: Genesis 10:4 reads “Dodanim” instead of “Rodanim,” reflecting a textual variation in the name.

revisions.rationale: Unapplied companion note: retain Chronicles Hebrew and marker-free English, place note on the disputed final name, identify Masoretic Genesis rather than implying all Genesis forms read Dodanim, and preserve versional disagreement.
